item.title: Strong-coupling quantum optics in free space with holes in a Fermi sea
item.description:
Worth a look theory — Pauli blocking of inelastic recoil channels by identical fermions in a trap enables directed spontaneous emission and strong light-matter coupling with single-atom cooperativity 𝒞≥1 in free space.

Grade 0.481 · 1.7σ above the day's baseline · matched “cavity QED, atom-photon interfaces and quantum networks” · Hao Wang, Hayden C. Orth, Duo Xu, Emily J. Davis

Figure

Unidirectional emission patterns in real space and momentum space showing asymmetric spontaneous scattering induced by momentum kick 𝐤12 from coherent drive fields.

Asks

Can an antenna formed by the center-of-mass wavefunction of a single atom exhibit large cooperativity 𝒞≥1 in free space?

Before

A single point atom driven by a focused Gaussian mode with waist w0=λ had cooperativity bounded by 𝒞point≤3/2π2.

But

Single-excitation subspace; requires tight fermionic trap loading, Ω2R≫Ω1R,Γs1e, and Γs2g≳|𝛀s2|,|𝛀e|,ℏk122/2m.

Tools

Pauli blocking in a Fermi sea · Adiabatic elimination · Center-of-mass wavefunction engineering · Dressed multi-level atomic schemes

Abstract

Coherent and efficient light-matter interfaces between an atom and a single mode of the electromagnetic field are essential for quantum technologies. Traditionally, these systems employ optical cavities or waveguides to isolate a specific mode of light, but a more recent approach is to engineer antennas from ordered configurations of trapped ultracold atoms that exhibit controllable and directed scattering. In this work, we propose a method to engineer an antenna from the center-of-mass wavefunction of a single atom, which can produce directed emission and thereby exhibit strong coupling to a target mode of light in free space. We predict that the resulting single-atom cooperativity can be comparable to the current state of the art in optical cavity and waveguide QED experiments. Building on this approach, we show that a wavepacket antenna becomes a single-atom mirror in the linear response regime. We study the modified dipole-dipole interactions and band structure of chains of such emitters, which can exhibit sub- and superradiance at spacings much larger than the wavelength of the light. Extending our approach to multi-level atoms, we propose a method to achieve arbitrary spatial scattering from a single atom, including uni-directional spontaneous emission. Finally, we elucidate how our approach can enhance cooperative scattering in conventional arrays of tightly trapped atoms.

item.title: Engineering dissipation and control pulses for high-fidelity fault-tolerance quantum computing
item.description:
Worth a look new method — Two-photon dissipative confinement autonomously restores dephasing-induced leakage back to the logical cat-state subspace with restoration rate ΓR,1≈4κ2|α|2, yielding final population P−(tf)≈99.64% at tf=0.5/κa under pure dephasing κaϕ=κa.

Grade 0.479 · 1.7σ above the day's baseline · matched “Quantum information with Rydberg atoms” · Shao-Wei Xu, Zhe-Yuan Zhang, Yi-Tong Shi, Ye-Hong Chen, Yan Xia

Figure

Final target population P−(tf) (red curve) and time-averaged subspace leakage PLeak(Avg) (light-blue curve) plotted against total evolution time tf∈(0,1/κa] in the presence of pure dephasing.

Asks

How to design fast, high-fidelity state transfer protocols for dissipative cat-state qubits that are robust against systematic drive errors and suppress dephasing-induced leakage?

But

Numerical simulation only. Requires drive amplitude εd(t)≪2κ2|α|2 and operation within the bounded time window 12κ2|α|3≪tf≪1κa|α|2.

Tools

shortcut-to-adiabaticity (STA) via inverse engineering · two-photon dissipative confinement · Lindblad master equation simulations · effective two-level subspace mapping

Abstract

Cat-state qubits, a prominent class of bosonic encodings, offer a promising pathway toward hardware-efficient fault-tolerant quantum computing. In this manuscript, we propose an optimally robust control protocol for the cat-state qubits which are stabilized by engineering two-photon dissipation. By deriving an effective two-level description in the cat-state subspace and applying shortcut-to-adiabaticity via inverse engineering, we design a robust protocol to achieve fast and high-fidelity state transfer in the cat-state qubit. We analyze the sensitivity to systematic control errors and identify an optimal robustness condition that strongly suppresses errors induced by imperfections in the driving fields. Furthermore, we show that dissipative confinement efficiently suppresses leakage out of the cat-state subspace caused by the pure dephasing, highlighting an intrinsic advantage of dissipative-cat qubits. This work establishes a robust and leakage-suppressing framework for high-fidelity bosonic qubit control, offering a promising route toward scalable fault-tolerant quantum computing.

item.title: Distribution of light-matter quantum correlations with a temporally multiplexed solid-state quantum memory array
item.description:
Worth a look new result — Telecom-heralded single photons stored across 10 spatial cells and 6 temporal modes (60 spatio-temporal modes total) in a Pr3+:Y2SiO5 array yield a 60-fold enhancement in detected correlated photon rate over a 39.1 km metropolitan fiber link.

Grade 0.458 · 1.5σ above the day's baseline · matched “quantum memories and repeaters for long-distance links” · Aya Mneimneh, Susana Plascencia, Manuel Gundin, Jonathan Hänni, Samuele Grandi, Markus Teller, Hugues de Riedmatten

Figure

Heralding and coincidence rates as functions of the filled round-trip communication time and number of spatio-temporal modes, showing linear rate scaling up to 60 modes.

Asks

Can spatial and temporal multiplexing be combined in a solid-state quantum memory array to distribute light-matter quantum correlations over deployed metropolitan fiber?

But

Round-trip communication time is 393 μs; communication trials fill up to 15% of this window. Cross-correlations limited by control-pulse fluorescence noise and neighbor crosstalk between cells separated by 200 μm.

Tools

Pr³⁺:Y₂SiO₅ atomic frequency comb spin-wave memory · cavity-enhanced SPDC source · acousto-optic deflectors · superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors · 39.1 km deployed metropolitan fiber

Abstract

Multiplexed quantum memories increase the entanglement distribution rate in long-distance quantum repeater architectures by harnessing storage in several degrees of freedom. Here, we report on the distribution of light-matter quantum correlations using an array of time-multiplexed solid-state quantum memories. We store telecom-heralded single photons sequentially in up to ten memory cells using the full atomic frequency comb protocol with on-demand read-out in a Pr³⁺:Y₂SiO₅ crystal. Leveraging both spatial and temporal multiplexing, we demonstrate quantum correlations between the telecom photon and up to 60 spatio-temporal modes of the quantum memory array. We then transmit the heralding telecom photon over 39.1 km of deployed optical fiber in the Metropolitan Area of Barcelona. In a realistic scenario where the generation rate is limited by the two-way communication time, we show that up to 15 % of the $393 μs$ round-trip communication time is filled with communication trials, leading to a 60-fold enhancement in the rate of detected telecom photons correlated with the quantum memory array, compared to a single-mode memory. With increased storage times and efficiencies, our multiplexed quantum memory array will constitute the backbone of a long-distance quantum network, establishing remote entanglement at high rates.

item.title: Exact 1/4 mean-rung population and √2 continuum revival-time ratio in the anti-Jaynes--Cummings vertex at f_⋆=√barn+1
item.description:
Worth a look theory — At the working point f⋆=n‾+1 with zero detuning and zero Kerr, the collapsed mean-rung excited population of the anti-Jaynes--Cummings (AJC) vertex is exactly 1/4 (compared to 1/2 for the Jaynes--Cummings vertex), and the continuum revival-time ratio tRAJC/tRJC equals 2.

Grade 0.453 · 1.5σ above the day's baseline · matched “Quantum information with Rydberg atoms” · Onyango Stephen Okeyo

Figure

Collapsed mean-rung excited population plotted against f=ω/λ at n‾=16. The AJC population curve crosses exactly 1/4 at f⋆=17≈4.123, while the JC population is constant at 1/2 across all f.

Asks

How can the residual sum-frequency detuning of an isolated anti-Jaynes--Cummings vertex be used for reference-normalized differential sensing against the Jaynes--Cummings vertex?

But

Requires zero Kerr coupling χ=0, resonance ξ=0, and static transverse rate g0≪g1; isolated-vertex dynamics ignores parent Rabi-model virtual transitions when λ/ω is non-negligible.

Tools

Isolated AJC Hamiltonian analytics · Hilbert-space diagonalization · Poisson packet averaging · Floquet counter-rotating coupling engineering

Abstract

At atomic resonance the Jaynes--Cummings (JC) vertex of a single bosonic mode coupled to a two-level emitter is blind to f=ω/λ at zero detuning and Kerr; the anti-Jaynes--Cummings (AJC) vertex is not. We show that the mean-rung excited population of the AJC block equals exactly 1/4 at f_⋆=√barn+1, while the JC population at the same point is 1/2. The Poisson-averaged packet value at barn=16 is 0.24650, within 3.5×10⁻³ of the exact value, with the deviation reproduced by -barn/[16(barn+1)²]. At f_⋆ the modulation depth of the AJC inversion is 1/2 and the relative sensitivity of the continuum revival-time ratio r=t_R^AJC/t_R^JC is maximal with value 1/(2√barn+1). Full diagonalization on 2(n_max+1) states confirms the analytic values. The 1/4 value can be generated by Floquet-engineered counter-rotating coupling provided that the static transverse rate satisfies g₀≪g₁. Parameter translations for an ideal trapped-ion blue sideband and a flux-tunable circuit-QED coupler are reported.
